messages:
Anika: Heads up — design question: when the automatic fallback kicks in (latency spike / 5xx burst), what should the operator acknowledgement flow look like? Do we require a manual confirm to re-enable or just auto-heal after X minutes?
Jordan: my 2c: auto-heal with visibility + a big, reversible "pause fallback" button. ops should be able to stop the auto re-enable if they want.
Maya: Agree on visibility. Also want an audit trail showing what trigger fired (error rate vs latency) + sample requests that fell back.
Sam: +1. And quota signals — if fallback caused routing to a cheaper model, we need cost delta in the UI so PMs can see impact.
Lee: From infra side, we need a throttle on ack frequency. Don't spam ops with repeated ack prompts during a storm. A single consolidated notification per incident is enough.
Anika: Thinking of this flow: fallback triggers -> operator gets inbox item with 3 actions: [Acknowledge], [Pause auto-reenable], [Open incident details]. If no action within 10min, auto-reenable proceeds. Thoughts?
Jordan: Fine but 10min might be tight for slow-timezone ops. Maybe make threshold configurable per deployment. Also we should surface why fallback chose the target model (compatibility/quantization) in the details.
Maya: UX nit: show a quick diff line item: "latency: 95th -> fallback model 95th" and "quality proxy: rouge-ish eval delta" so stakeholders can triage quicker.
Sam: Example of the inbox payload for operator, sketch:
```
{
  "incident_id": "inc_2026_03_22_42",
  "trigger": "5xx_rate>3%",
  "fallback_policy": "soft-sample-10%",
  "actions": ["ack", "pause_reenable", "open_playbook"]
}
```
Lee: ops-bot should auto-attach a short replay: 5 sample requests + responses that were rerouted. That helps debugging without running the replay tool.
ops-bot: I can generate a compact replay when a fallback event is created. Will include request IDs + small scrubbed context. :robot_face:
Anika: Audit requirements — compliance wants an immutable record: who acked, when, what config changed. That implies we need writeable audit logs and export in CSV/JSON.
Maya: Also add a rollback action in UI to force revert to previous rollout if quality regressions are detected. But make it gated (require 2 approvers for prod).
Jordan: For the console, propose 2 new panes: 1) incident inbox (pending operator actions), 2) fallback timeline (history + linked traces). Both should support filters: model, route, trigger type.
Sam: Telemetry: attach a tag to all tokens served during fallback with `fallback_reason` and `fallback_id` so cost/quality metrics can be sliced afterwards.
Lee: We also need backend rate-limits for the ack API so a noisy script can't ack/unack repeatedly. Enforce RBAC: only ops or release managers can pause auto-reenable.
Anika: UX wording question: "Pause auto-reenable" vs "Hold until manual resume" — which is clearer?
Maya: "Hold until manual resume" reads clearer to me. More explicit.
Jordan: Agreed. Short label: "Hold until resumed" for the button.
Anika: Final checklist for implementation: 1) operator inbox item + actions, 2) replay attachment (scrubbed), 3) audit log entry (immutable), 4) reenable timer configurable per environment, 5) RBAC on pause/resume, 6) cost/quality deltas in incident view. Anything missing?
Sam: Add: exportable incident bundle (logs + 5 samples + telemetry link) for postmortem.
Lee: Add: hysteresis on reenable (require N stable minutes without trigger).
Maya: And add an "explain why" link that surfaces the fallback decision tree (thresholds, model mapping). helps SREs onboard.
Anika: Great. I'll prototype the inbox UI and a compact incident JSON for the API. Will post a mock next week. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Jordan: Thanks — ping if you want a quick review of the mock.
ops-bot: Logged: fallback_event inc_2026_03_22_42 created by auto-controller. Linked: telemetry://fallback/inc_2026_03_22_42
Maya: If anyone wants to test flows, we can run a chaos sim on staging next Tuesday.
Sam: I'll add telemetry slices to the sim.
Lee: I'll add RBAC checks to the ack endpoint before the sim.
Anika: sweet — end of thread for now.
